explanation: Public affection beyond simple hand-holding is traditionally frowned upon in Thailand; kissing and hugging in public, even between married couples, can draw stares or social disapproval. Attitudes are loosening somewhat, especially among younger couples in Bangkok, where hand-holding or an arm around a partner is now common, but overt kissing or prolonged hugging in public remains discouraged almost everywhere, and temple grounds are stricter still.
local_tip: Holding hands is generally fine, but save kissing and prolonged hugging for private spaces, and avoid any physical affection at all on temple grounds.
regional_note: Younger couples in Bangkok and other urban centers are increasingly open about hand-holding, but kissing or hugging in public is still discouraged nationwide, and temples hold a stricter standard than everyday public spaces.

also_check.note: Public kissing and affection between couples is widely accepted and normal.
Public displays of affection are illegal and can result in fines or arrest.
PDA is generally avoided in public, though hand-holding is increasingly accepted among young couples.
